11   Q.          What is the test year that SPS uses in establishing its revenue requirement?

12   A.          SPS uses a future test year (FTY), a 12-month period of projected revenues, expenses, and

13               asset and liability balances projected for when SPS expects new rates will go into effect.

14               The future test year period SPS selected is December 1, 2026 to November 30, 2027. To

15               get to that future test year, the utility starts with actual recorded amounts for revenues,

16               expenses, plant asset balances and liabilities from a recently completed 12-month “base

17               period” (the base period in this case is July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025), forecasts amounts

18               for a “linkage period” from the end of the base period to the beginning of the future test

19               year, then forecasts revenues, expenses, and asset and liability balances for the 12 months

20               of the future test year. The future test year method contrasts with the historical test year

 3                                       Legacy Meter Amortization

 4   Q.      Please describe SPS’s request to record a regulatory asset for legacy meter costs.

 5   A.      SPS is retiring older electric meters as it modernizes its grid with Advanced Metering

6            Infrastructure (AMI). In case 22-00178-UT, the Commission approved recovery of the

7            undepreciated balance of legacy meters but did not allow SPS to earn a return on that asset.

8            In the final order for that case, the commission stated:

 9                   The Commission hereby approves of SPS’ recovery of the undepreciated
10                   balance of legacy meters that have been removed from service but does not
11                   approve of a return on that asset. The undepreciated balance of legacy
12                   meters removed from service shall be removed from the rate base in the next
13                   rate case, and placed into a regulatory asset that earns no interest. The
14                   recovery period of this asset will be decided in the Company’s next rate
15                   case, but in no event will the amortization period be longer than ten years. 7

22           revenue requirement. SPS states: “SPS is bearing the financial cost of carrying the

 4   Q.      What is Staff’s recommendation regarding the legacy meter regulatory asset and

 5           amortization period?

8            of $4,039,393. In its Order in Docket 22-00178-UT, the Commission ordered the

 9           amortization period not be longer than ten years. 10 Based upon the public interest in

10           affordable electricity rates and given that there is a window of acceptable amortization

11           periods, Staff believe that it is best to use a longer, five-year period which allows the

12           company to recoup costs in timely manner but also not burden rate payers with higher

13           costs. Additionally, in that case, SPS itself requested a ten-year amortization period for the

14           Legacy Meter undepreciated balance. 11
